pages.name: goat-processors
pages.shows: a test vector replayed step by step on a plan view, with its trace records
pages.title: goat-processors
pages.tagline: Correlation, fusion, filtering and track quality, with every decision traced.
pages.lede: Each function is a written specification, packs of settings and test vectors. Seven engines, written apart in seven languages, reproduce every vector exactly, down to the record of each test they run.

pages.name: goat-transformers
pages.shows: a conversion played byte by byte by the engine built to WebAssembly
pages.title: goat-transformers: convert a message from any format to any other
pages.tagline: Any message format to any other. Every format is a data file.
pages.lede: A drone's 25-byte Remote ID broadcast becomes a Cursor on Target event for a tactical map. No engine holds code for either format: each is a pack, a text file with one line for each field, and seven engines in seven languages read the same packs and must agree byte for byte.

numbers.how: each one a pack from a public source
all seven engines match every one
the engine as WebAssembly, in this page

pages.name: open-billie
pages.shows: a real frame decoded in the first screen
pages.title: Open Billie
pages.tagline: Any sensor in, one track record, three standard formats out.
pages.lede: Open Billie prepares a node, builds a small package for each sensor (a kid), and publishes its data, normalized, as CoT, ASTERIX CAT062 or SAPIENT through Zenoh. The kid decodes; the shared translator writes the format.

pages.name: first-bite
pages.title: first-bite: binary messages off the wire, decoded and published
pages.tagline: Binary messages off the wire, decoded, for those you authorise.
pages.lede: It listens on a tap or a mirror port, local or tunnelled (ERSPAN/GRE), decodes fixed-layout binary messages against a dictionary, and publishes each one as a record of typed values. It never transmits on the capture interface.

numbers.l: resident while replaying a 145 MB capture
the portable mind, needing only glibc

pages.name: saltlick
pages.shows: a directory session recorded against a real instance
pages.title: saltlick
pages.tagline: Advisory, never authoritative. Being listed grants access to nothing.
pages.lede: A directory where an organization publishes its own interconnection capability, so that two organizations can check compatibility before they build a link. It holds signed pointers, not permissions. The reader checks every signature and digest against keys it bound outside the directory.

pages.name: goat-client
pages.shows: the real daemon, CLI and handshake, replayed
pages.title: goat-client
pages.tagline: One signed file, and the device is on the goat network.
pages.lede: A daemon, a desktop GUI and a command line for Linux, macOS and Windows, with iOS, iPadOS and Android shells. It takes a bundle signed by an offline certificate authority, checks the signature, and brings up the outer WireGuard tunnel, the inner NetBird mesh, or both.

pages.name: goatrodeo
pages.title: goatrodeo
pages.tagline: Games and toys that run on a goat data fabric.
pages.lede: Each one is fun to play and publishes real events while you play it. Air Defenders is the first: a browser arcade game, solo or co-op, that runs on a laptop with one Go command.

numbers.l: the solo game, one HTML file

pages.name: open-entity-gateway
pages.shows: what the gateway prints for one record
pages.title: open-entity-gateway
pages.tagline: Bridges between the goat fabric and vendor systems.
pages.lede: Each bridge is its own package that speaks one vendor's software kit: Anduril Lattice and Picogrid ECN today. A mapping file says how a record becomes a track; the bridge sends it in the vendor's form.

numbers.l: vendor SDKs installed by core CI

pages.name: zagros-moon-pod
pages.title: zagros-moon-pod
pages.tagline: A small bundle you run on your own host to exchange data with a goat fabric, both ways.
pages.lede: A Zenoh router with mutual TLS that may write only your slot, an observe-only audit sink, and a mesh client on the host. Today it is for learning: rung 2 of the goat learner ladder, joined to the zagros sandbox, not in operational use.

numbers.l: allow rules over a default deny

pages.name: goat-cloud
pages.shows: an ownership register: every cloud resource has an owner
pages.title: goat-cloud: every cloud resource has an owner
pages.tagline: Every cloud resource has an owner, a purpose and a lifetime that anyone can look up.
pages.lede: Developers deploy from their own repositories with no central gate and no ticket. Each night a scan finds what has no owner or has outlived its stated expiry; its owner is warned, and it is removed.

numbers.l: facts on every resource: project, environment, managing tool, lifecycle, repository, and an expiry when it is not meant to last
deployment tools take part on equal terms: Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, CloudFormation, Serverless Framework, CDK, SAM, Copilot
tests pass from a fresh clone; none needs a cloud credential
resources and findings in one scan of the synthetic demo estate, from one command

pages.name: goatrope
pages.shows: a rope figure drawn by `build.py`, state drawn rather than colored
pages.title: goatrope
pages.tagline: Tie distant machines to one link, or tap the link they share.
pages.lede: goatrope takes a copy of one network link, from a tap device, a switch mirror port or its own inline tap on a small computer, and records it, sends on what you name, or relays named datagrams. The relay joins distant sites over the mesh they already share, or through a declared boundary point when a site stands outside it; it is work in progress. One file declares what it does. It runs with nothing else of ours installed.

frames out of a listen port: install, traffic, attempts to send, restarts
pings through the bridge while it is deployed again

pages.name: goat
pages.title: goat: a self-hosted data fabric
pages.tagline: A self-hosted data fabric that keeps working when the network around it fails.
pages.lede: goat joins people, machines and services across sites into one network. They publish and subscribe to data, and access is decided by who they are, not where they sit. A device that has joined keeps talking to its peers directly, with or without the cloud.

numbers.l: to rehearse a full standup of the example environment on a laptop: 5 components on 4 machines, 14 checks

decision records in the repository, one per design decision, never rewritten
the largest goatbuilder release binary; one file per platform, four platforms

pages.name: fieldkit-feeds
pages.shows: Fieldkit Feeds, a service inside goatstuff
pages.title: Fieldkit Feeds: send fabric data to a system, and bring a system's data in
pages.tagline: Send fabric data to the systems that need it, and bring their data in. A tactical admin switches it on.
pages.lede: An operator picks a topic and the system that should receive it, or names what a system sends and the standard it uses. A tactical admin for the site switches the feed on; anyone else's request waits for one. Each feed shows one word for its health, its counters, the exact command it runs and who did what.

numbers.l: actions on a feed: approve, decline, pause, resume, renew, remove, check. Fieldkit allows at most eight
direct dependency, the Postgres driver; no JavaScript framework, no package manager, no build step for the page
static Linux binaries, x86-64 and arm64, page included: the hosts the fleet runs on

pages.name: hello-galaxy
pages.title: Hello Galaxy
pages.tagline: 17 small repositories. Each answers one question about goat by running it.
pages.lede: Every repository is a short runbook per step and one script that drives the real tools, prints what happens, and says plainly what it does not run. Pick the question you have, clone that repository, and run one command.
